frozenBandRootCauseHypothesis.statement: Layout metrics are frozen across 0-914.98px and again across 915px-infinity because the clone's CSS contains exactly ONE width-dependent decision (which of two subtrees to display), and every box inside each subtree is pinned to a pixel value resolved at a single observation width. There is no continuous reflow mechanism, only a two-position switch.

hiddenColumnRootCauseHypothesis.statement: At 1100px on /pricing the clone hides 503 nodes the source shows because a per-node display:none is synthesized for the band (min-width: 1024px) and (max-width: 1231.98px). That band's UPPER edge is a pure arithmetic midpoint between two probe samples 416px apart, invented by hiddenRanges(); the source's real transition lies in (1024, 1100]. The measurement at 1024 was CORRECT — the interpolation from it is what is wrong — and this rule kind is the one kind the post-emit truth check is structurally unable to verify.

hiddenColumnRootCauseHypothesis.orthogonalContributorAtTheSameWidth: Even with the hidden band removed, 1100px would still be wrong: the desktop variant renders 1440px-pinned boxes with no overflow management (see layoutInferenceResponsiveness.widthMinMaxAndOverflow), which the 28.5B sweep measured as maxContentRight 1440 in a 1100px viewport. The band causes the MISSING columns; the pinning causes the CLIPPED/overflowing ones. Both must be addressed.

additionalFindingsForPlanning: The probe's 390px row is taken at DPR 1 / isMobile false / desktop UA (src/observer/layout-probe.ts:226-235), while the deep mobile observation is DPR 3 / touch / mobile UA (src/observer/types.ts:127-134). The two 390px measurements are not the same page state; any future mobile-side inference must not assume they are.

The probe re-measures the SAME parked element references after each resize (src/observer/layout-probe.ts:121, :139-146). A framework that replaces nodes on resize marks them disconnected and they read v=0 at that width AND every wider width, which then fails the vAt(truth)==1 test at src/reconstruction/layout-inference.ts:362 and emits nothing. That failure mode is safe (silently no rule), but it also means node churn silently shrinks the fluid tier with no counter distinguishing it.

settle() between resizes is 2 rAF + 250ms (src/observer/layout-probe.ts:181-191, src/observer/types.ts:1108), versus SETTLE_MS = 1200 for the deep observation (src/observer/types.ts:175). A slow resize handler could be measured mid-transition.

MAX_LAYOUT_RULES = 2000 and MAX_MATCHED_RULES_PER_ELEMENT = 32 cap the authored channel (src/observer/types.ts:480-486, enforced src/observer/collect-dom.ts:335-340, :399-421). On a large site the authored index truncates silently.

The 'flex' shorthand is absent from STYLE_WHITELIST (only flex-grow/flex-shrink/flex-basis are present, src/observer/types.ts:292-294) although it IS in LAYOUT_RULE_PROPERTIES (:442). Not responsive-critical on its own, but it is an asymmetry between the two channels.

ResponsiveModel.inferredBreakpoints is schema-present and ALWAYS empty (src/sitespec/types.ts:1604-1609). If 28.5C introduces measured breakpoints, that field is the intended home, but the docstring at :1599-1602 requires them to be labeled as the renderer's claim, not the IR's observation.

The only operator control over responsive behaviour today is --breakpoint <px> (src/cli-reconstruct.ts:61-66, :94, :278). There is no way to add probe widths, disable the responsive-hidden tier, or widen a band from any CLI.
